Logistic structural mean model

Source: R/lsmm.R
lsmm.Rd

Function to estimate the double logistic structural mean model (LSMM) of Vansteelandt and Goetghebeur (2003) by the generalized method of moments (GMM), as described by Clarke et al. (2015).

Usage

lsmm(
  formula,
  instruments,
  data,
  subset,
  na.action,
  contrasts = NULL,
  t0 = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

formula, instruments

formula specification(s) of the regression relationship and the instruments. Either instruments is missing and formula has three parts as in y ~ x1 + x2 | z1 + z2 + z3 (recommended) or formula is y ~ x1 + x2 and instruments is a one-sided formula ~ z1 + z2 + z3 (only for backward compatibility).

data

an optional data frame containing the variables in the model. By default the variables are taken from the environment of the formula.

subset

an optional vector specifying a subset of observations to be used in fitting the model.

na.action

a function that indicates what should happen when the data contain NAs. The default is set by the na.action option.

contrasts

an optional list. See the contrasts.arg of stats::model.matrix().

t0

A vector of starting values for the gmm optimizer. This should have length equal to the number of association model parameters (the intercept, exposures, instruments, and covariates), plus the number of exposures and covariates, plus 1. By default the starting values are the estimates from a logistic regression for the association model and from a two-stage residual inclusion logistic regression for the causal model.

...

further arguments passed to or from other methods.

Value

An object of class "lsmm". A list with the following items:

fit

The object from the second step gmm::gmm() fit.

corci

The causal odds ratio/s of the exposure/s and the corresponding 95% confidence interval limits.

ey0ci

The estimate of the exposure free potential outcome mean and its 95% confidence interval limits.

covariates

A character vector of the names of any covariates.

Details

The LSMM is $$\mathrm{logit}\, E(Y \mid X, Z) - \mathrm{logit}\, E\{Y(0) \mid X, Z\} = \psi X,$$ so that \(\exp(\psi)\) is a causal odds ratio among the exposed. Unlike the additive and multiplicative structural mean models, the LSMM also requires a model for the observed outcome mean, the association model, which here is a logistic regression of the outcome on the exposures, the instruments, and any covariates. The association model and the causal model are fitted jointly by two-step GMM. The moment conditions for the association model are its logistic regression score equations, and those for the causal model are that the predicted exposure-free potential outcome is mean independent of the instruments. The initial weight matrix is block diagonal, with blocks equal to the inverse of the crossproduct of the regressors of each model, and the second step uses the optimal weight matrix. This is the same estimator as the ivlsmm command in the Stata package ivonesamplemr.

Covariates are adjusted for by including them in both the exposure and the instrument parts of the formula, as in y ~ x + w | z1 + z2 + w. They are then included in both the association model and the causal model, as in ivlsmm.

References

Clarke PS, Palmer TM, Windmeijer F. Estimating structural mean models with multiple instrumental variables using the Generalised Method of Moments. Statistical Science, 2015, 30, 1, 96-117. doi:10.1214/14-STS503

Vansteelandt S, Goetghebeur E. Causal inference with generalized structural mean models. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B, 2003, 65, 4, 817-835. doi:10.1046/j.1369-7412.2003.00417.x

Vansteelandt S, Bowden J, Babanezhad M, Goetghebeur E. On instrumental variables estimation of causal odds ratios. Statistical Science, 2011, 26, 3, 403-422. doi:10.1214/11-STS360

Examples

# Multiple instrument example
set.seed(123456)
n    <- 1000
psi0 <- 0.5
G1   <- rbinom(n, 2, 0.5)
G2   <- rbinom(n, 2, 0.3)
G3   <- rbinom(n, 2, 0.4)
U    <- runif(n)
pX   <- plogis(0.7*G1 + G2 - G3 + U)
X    <- rbinom(n, 1, pX)
pY   <- plogis(-2 + psi0*X + U)
Y    <- rbinom(n, 1, pY)
dat  <- data.frame(G1, G2, G3, X, Y)
fit  <- lsmm(Y ~ X | G1 + G2 + G3, data = dat)
fit
